evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by URL inherently requires a game and its URL to exist (creation of a game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round presupposes a game/session context (a game must exist to start a round).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Seeing all items for the session inherently depends on items having been created/added during the session.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that items exist (were added or entered into a round) before selection can occur.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items presumes the existence of a game/session context to which items are added.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item requires that the item already exists (i.e., items must have been added previously).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item presupposes that items exist in the list (they must have been created/added first).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates presumes that estimators have joined and given estimates in a round; it depends on round and participant setup.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that multiple estimates exist from a round (requires round and estimators to be present).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatically filling the estimate depends on estimators participating and showing cards in a round (requires round/estimators).

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate is part of the post-estimation flow and requires an estimation round to have taken place.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story inherently depends on that story having been estimated earlier in the session.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories can be implemented as a standalone feature (does not inherently require another specific backlog story to be implemented first).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste import is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games presupposes that previous games exist (i.e., games must have been created/played previously).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript inherently requires that a game and its transcript exist (game/session creation and recording).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires that the transcript exists (i.e., viewing/recording of transcripts must be available first).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting CSV of a transcript depends on transcripts existing for a game (requires transcript/view capability).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presupposes that games exist to be deleted (game creation/storage required).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application
evaluations.rationale: Creating an account is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently depends on accounts existing (account creation must be available).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presupposes that an account exists (account creation required).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that the account exists (depends on account creation).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a self-contained presentation feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder functionality requires that accounts with email addresses exist (depends on account creation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing the card set is a configuration capability and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators presumes the invitation mechanism and game context exist (depends on invite and game creation stories).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via a URL presupposes that an invite/URL has been generated (depends on the invite mechanism).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the item being estimated depends on a round being started and an item being selected/entered.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: This requires that items for the session have been added/entered; it depends on item creation for the session.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Detecting that an estimator has given an estimate requires estimators to have joined and be participating in a round.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This behavior inherently depends on an estimation round and estimators giving estimates (round and participants must exist).

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Allowing change until the last selection requires the round/draw mechanics and participant estimates to be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Providing access to prior estimates can be implemented as a standalone feature (does not inherently require a specific other backlog item to be implemented first).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing who gave which estimates depends on estimators and current-round estimates existing (requires participant/join and round features).

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog items being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-reset on all estimates depends on both the timer feature and the ability to detect when all participants have played estimates.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling prior rounds presupposes that prior rounds and their data exist (requires round creation/storage).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining a stable card order is a self-contained UI/behaviour decision and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This behavior requires the draw/round lifecycle and detection of draw completion to be implemented (depends on estimation flow).

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a presentation feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting implementation quality and does not inherently depend on other specific backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is self-contained and does not inherently require other backlog stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a developer task that can be implemented independently and does not inherently require other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is an implementation quality and not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a cross-cutting requirement and does not inherently depend on other specific backlog items.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a quality requirement and can be implemented independently of other stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a platform/encoding requirement and does not inherently require other backlog stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error pages are a presentation/UX feature and do not inherently require other backlog stories to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Data anonymization requirement can be implemented independently and does not inherently require another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Providing usage metrics is a standalone reporting feature and does not inherently require another single backlog story to be implemented first.
